svg.aria-label: Experiment 02: four hundred concurrent bookings compete for a single flight of capacity 314. A pessimistic row lock serialises them, so exactly 314 reserve and 86 are cleanly rejected. The reserved count reaches capacity and stops — it never exceeds it.

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
text.tspan: · many bookings, one scarce seat, never oversold

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The reservation is not a simple UPDATE: it is the inventory side of the choreography saga, guarded by a pessimistic row lock inside a single transaction.

svg.text: Booking creation returns 201 PENDING immediately; the reservation resolves asynchronously, so the outcome is measured after the burst drains.

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Falsifiable: reserved_count > total_capacity at any point, winners != floor(C/q), or a booking that neither reserves nor rejects.
